facts.raw_span: A 58-year-old woman presented with a 3-year history of a right-breast lump
no family history of breast cancer
had been menopausal for 5 years
denied eating frogs or snakes
recalled drinking impure water
migratory discomfort and pain in the right axilla and upper-outer quadrant
a mobile lump was palpated
a hypoechoic, tubular structure with surrounding increased echogenicity, measuring 5.0 × 1.7 × 0.7 cm (BIRADS 4b)
an oval, low-echo mass with well-delineated contours, measuring 1.8 × 1.2 × 0.4 cm (BIRADS 4a) and closely abutting the pectoralis major
two small hypoechoic masses in the fat layer, measuring 0.5 × 0.3 cm and 0.3 × 0.2 cm
No obvious blood-flow signals were detected within any of these lesions on color Doppler flow imaging

concepts.why: The patient's 3-year history of a right-breast lump, combined with the ultrasonography findings of a hypoechoic, tubular structure and an oval, low-echo mass, are consistent with invasive ductal carcinoma.
The mobile lump palpated on examination and the small hypoechoic masses in the fat layer on ultrasonography are consistent with fibroadenoma.
The ultrasonography findings of a hypoechoic, tubular structure and small hypoechoic masses in the fat layer are consistent with phyllodes tumor.

The patient's history of migratory discomfort and pain in the right axilla and upper-outer quadrant, combined with the ultrasonography findings of small hypoechoic masses in the fat layer, are consistent with fat necrosis.
The mobile lump palpated on examination and the absence of obvious blood-flow signals on color Doppler flow imaging are consistent with breast cyst.

The patient's history of migratory discomfort and pain in the right axilla and upper-outer quadrant, combined with the ultrasonography findings of a hypoechoic, tubular structure, are consistent with inflammatory breast cancer.
The patient's history of migratory discomfort and pain in the right axilla and upper-outer quadrant, combined with the palpation of a mobile lump, are consistent with mastitis.
The patient's history of drinking impure water is consistent with waterborne illness.

rationales.F01: A 3-year history of a right-breast lump is more typical of a benign condition, but still possible in invasive ductal carcinoma.
rationales.F02: No family history of breast cancer makes invasive ductal carcinoma less likely.
rationales.F03: Menopause increases the risk of breast cancer, making invasive ductal carcinoma more likely.
rationales.F05: Drinking impure water is a risk factor for waterborne illness, but not directly related to breast cancer.
rationales.F06: Migratory discomfort and pain in the right axilla and upper-outer quadrant could be indicative of several conditions, including breast cancer and mastitis.
rationales.F08: A hypoechoic, tubular structure with surrounding increased echogenicity is highly suggestive of invasive ductal carcinoma.
rationales.F09: An oval, low-echo mass with well-delineated contours is highly suggestive of invasive ductal carcinoma.

frontier_selector.rationale: The presence of a hypoechoic, tubular structure with surrounding increased echogenicity and an oval, low-echo mass with well-delineated contours, both with BIRADS 4 lesions, strongly supports invasive ductal carcinoma, despite some findings also being compatible with Phyllodes tumor.
